source_arguments.name: GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.biprojectiveCorrection_coeff_isWeightedHomogeneous
source_arguments.statement:
theorem biprojectiveCorrection_coeff_isWeightedHomogeneous (U V : K[X]) (k : ℕ) :
    ((Polynomial.C
          (MvPolynomial.X (biprojLeftInfinity : BiprojVar m n) *
            MvPolynomial.X (biprojRightInfinity : BiprojVar m n)) *
        (1 + (U * V).map MvPolynomial.C)).coeff k).IsWeightedHomogeneous
      biprojectiveWeight (1, 1)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem biprojectiveCorrection_coeff_isWeightedHomogeneous (U V : K[X]) (k : ℕ) :
    ((Polynomial.C
          (MvPolynomial.X (biprojLeftInfinity : BiprojVar m n) *
            MvPolynomial.X (biprojRightInfinity : BiprojVar m n)) *
        (1 + (U * V).map MvPolynomial.C)).coeff k).IsWeightedHomogeneous
      biprojectiveWeight (1, 1)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  rw [Polynomial.coeff_C_mul]
  have hAlpha : ((MvPolynomial.X (biprojLeftInfinity : BiprojVar m n) :
      MvPolynomial (BiprojVar m n) K)).IsWeightedHomogeneous
      biprojectiveWeight (1, 0) := by
    simpa [biprojLeftInfinity, biprojectiveWeight] using
      (MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_X (R := K) biprojectiveWeight
        (biprojLeftInfinity : BiprojVar m n))
  have hBeta : ((MvPolynomial.X (biprojRightInfinity : BiprojVar m n) :
      MvPolynomial (BiprojVar m n) K)).IsWeightedHomogeneous
      biprojectiveWeight (0, 1) := by
    simpa [biprojRightInfinity, biprojectiveWeight] using
      (MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_X (R := K) biprojectiveWeight
        (biprojRightInfinity : BiprojVar m n))
  have hScalar : ((1 + (U * V).map
      (MvPolynomial.C : K →+* MvPolynomial (BiprojVar m n) K)).coeff k).IsWeightedHomogeneous
      biprojectiveWeight 0 := by
    rw [Polynomial.coeff_add, Polynomial.coeff_map]
    rcases k with rfl | k
    · simpa using
        (MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_one K biprojectiveWeight).add
          (MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_C biprojectiveWeight ((U * V).coeff 0))
    · simpa [Polynomial.coeff_one] using
        (MvPolynomial.isWeightedHomogeneous_C biprojectiveWeight ((U * V).coeff (k + 1)))
  simpa using (hAlpha.mul hBeta).mul hScalar

source_arguments.name: GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.neg_le_secondDifference_of_weighted
source_arguments.statement:
theorem neg_le_secondDifference_of_weighted {f : ℝ → ℝ} {X s δ : ℝ} (hX : 0 < X) (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    (hsX : s ≤ X / 2) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hf : 0 ≤ f X)
    (hp : Real.sqrt (X + s) * f (X + s) ≤ Real.sqrt X * f X + δ * s)
    (hm : Real.sqrt (X - s) * f (X - s) ≤ Real.sqrt X * f X + δ * s) :
    -(2 * (δ * s / Real.sqrt X) + 2 * (s / X) * (f X + δ * s / Real.sqrt X))
      ≤ secondDifference f X s
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem neg_le_secondDifference_of_weighted {f : ℝ → ℝ} {X s δ : ℝ} (hX : 0 < X) (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    (hsX : s ≤ X / 2) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hf : 0 ≤ f X)
    (hp : Real.sqrt (X + s) * f (X + s) ≤ Real.sqrt X * f X + δ * s)
    (hm : Real.sqrt (X - s) * f (X - s) ≤ Real.sqrt X * f X + δ * s) :
    -(2 * (δ * s / Real.sqrt X) + 2 * (s / X) * (f X + δ * s / Real.sqrt X))
      ≤ secondDifference f X s
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hfwd := le_of_weighted_le_forward hX hs hδ hf hp
  have hbwd := le_of_weighted_le_backward hX hs hsX hδ hf hm
  unfold secondDifference
  have hA : f X + δ * s / Real.sqrt X - f X = δ * s / Real.sqrt X := by ring
  nlinarith [hfwd, hbwd, hA]

multiple of `s`, with constant `2δ/√X + 2(f X + δ√X/2)/X`.  Only the kernel's *first* moment is
then needed — no second moment enters. -/

source_arguments.statement:
theorem hsSqRe_sum_le_weighted {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (W : ι → Matrix d d ℂ)
    (hc : ∑ i, ‖c i‖ = 1) :
    hsSqRe (∑ i, c i • W i) ≤ ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * hsSqRe (W i)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem hsSqRe_sum_le_weighted {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (W : ι → Matrix d d ℂ)
    (hc : ∑ i, ‖c i‖ = 1) :
    hsSqRe (∑ i, c i • W i) ≤ ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * hsSqRe (W i)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hentry : ∀ a b : d, (∑ i, c i • W i) b a = ∑ i, c i • W i b a := by
    intro a b
    simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
  have hstep : ∀ a b : d, ‖(∑ i, c i • W i) b a‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2 := by
    intro a b
    rw [hentry a b]
    exact norm_sum_sq_le_weighted (E := ℂ) c (fun i => W i b a) hc
  rw [hsSqRe_eq_sum]
  have hbound : ∑ a, ∑ b, ‖(∑ i, c i • W i) b a‖ ^ 2
      ≤ ∑ a, ∑ b, ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2 :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hstep a b
  refine le_trans hbound (le_of_eq ?_)
  have hR : ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * hsSqRe (W i) = ∑ i, ∑ a, ∑ b, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2 := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [hsSqRe_eq_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.mul_sum _ _ _
  rw [hR]
  calc ∑ a, ∑ b, ∑ i, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2
      = ∑ a, ∑ i, ∑ b, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2 :=
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => Finset.sum_comm
    _ = ∑ i, ∑ a, ∑ b, ‖c i‖ * ‖W i b a‖ ^ 2 := Finset.sum_comm

source_arguments.statement:
theorem strictlyPositiveWeightedFiniteCircleMeasure_rajchman_iff
    (M : {μ : Measure UnitAddCircle // IsFiniteMeasure μ})
    (g : ContinuousStrictlyPositiveCircleWeight) :
    IsAddCircleRajchman (strictlyPositiveWeightedFiniteCircleMeasure M g) ↔
      IsAddCircleRajchman (M : Measure UnitAddCircle)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem strictlyPositiveWeightedFiniteCircleMeasure_rajchman_iff
    (M : {μ : Measure UnitAddCircle // IsFiniteMeasure μ})
    (g : ContinuousStrictlyPositiveCircleWeight) :
    IsAddCircleRajchman (strictlyPositiveWeightedFiniteCircleMeasure M g) ↔
      IsAddCircleRajchman (M : Measure UnitAddCircle)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  constructor
  · intro hweighted
    let W : {μ : Measure UnitAddCircle // IsAddCircleRajchman μ} :=
      ⟨strictlyPositiveWeightedFiniteCircleMeasure M g, hweighted⟩
    have hback := continuousWeightedCircleMeasure_isAddCircleRajchman W g.invNonnegative
    have heq : continuousWeightedCircleMeasure W g.invNonnegative =
        (M : Measure UnitAddCircle) := by
      unfold continuousWeightedCircleMeasure W
      change ((M : Measure UnitAddCircle).withDensity
          (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal (g.1 z))).withDensity
            (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((g.1 z)⁻¹)) = (M : Measure UnitAddCircle)
      rw [show (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((g.1 z)⁻¹)) =
          fun z => (ENNReal.ofReal (g.1 z))⁻¹ by
        funext z
        exact ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos (g.2 z)]
      exact MeasureTheory.withDensity_inv_same
        (g.1.continuous.measurable.ennreal_ofReal)
        (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun z => by simp [g.2 z])
        (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top)
    rwa [heq] at hback
  · intro hM
    let MR : {μ : Measure UnitAddCircle // IsAddCircleRajchman μ} :=
      ⟨(M : Measure UnitAddCircle), hM⟩
    change IsAddCircleRajchman
      (continuousWeightedCircleMeasure MR g.nonnegative)
    exact continuousWeightedCircleMeasure_isAddCircleRajchman MR g.nonnegative

source_arguments.name: RHTower.deningerUnweighted_iteratedFDeriv_bound
source_arguments.statement:
theorem deningerUnweighted_iteratedFDeriv_bound {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f) (c : ℝ)
    (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    Real.exp (c * x) * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ b f x‖
      ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (b + 1), (b.choose j : ℝ) * |c| ^ j
          * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem deningerUnweighted_iteratedFDeriv_bound {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f) (c : ℝ)
    (b : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    Real.exp (c * x) * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ b f x‖
      ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (b + 1), (b.choose j : ℝ) * |c| ^ j
          * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hg : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) :=
    (deningerExpWeightC_contDiff c).mul hf
  have hcancel : (fun t => deningerExpWeightC (-c) t * (deningerExpWeightC c t * f t)) = f := by
    funext t
    rw [deningerExpWeightC, deningerExpWeightC, ← mul_assoc, ← Complex.ofReal_mul,
      ← Real.exp_add]
    have hzero : -c * t + c * t = 0 := by ring
    rw [hzero, Real.exp_zero, Complex.ofReal_one, one_mul]
  have hbd := deningerWeighted_iteratedFDeriv_bound hg (-c) b x
  rw [hcancel] at hbd
  have hmul : Real.exp (c * x) * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ b f x‖
      ≤ Real.exp (c * x) * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (b + 1), (b.choose j : ℝ)
          * (|(-c)| ^ j * Real.exp (-c * x))
          * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖ :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbd (Real.exp_pos _).le
  refine le_trans hmul (le_of_eq ?_)
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  have hexp : Real.exp (c * x) * Real.exp (-c * x) = 1 := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    have : c * x + -c * x = 0 := by ring
    rw [this, Real.exp_zero]
  calc Real.exp (c * x) * ((b.choose j : ℝ) * (|(-c)| ^ j * Real.exp (-c * x))
        * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖)
      = ((b.choose j : ℝ) * |(-c)| ^ j
          * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖)
        * (Real.exp (c * x) * Real.exp (-c * x)) := by ring
    _ = (b.choose j : ℝ) * |c| ^ j
          * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (b - j) (fun t => deningerExpWeightC c t * f t) x‖ := by
        rw [hexp, mul_one, abs_neg]

### The two different Garland theorems

1. **Garland (1971), *A finiteness theorem for `K₂` of a number field*, Ann. of Math. 94.**  This is
   the paper the parent card cites, and it does prove `K₂(𝒪_F)` finite.  Its method is
   **archimedean**: Riemannian geometry and harmonic forms on the symmetric space, establishing
   `H²(SL_n(𝔬), ℝ) = 0` for `n > 6`.  It is *not* the combinatorial building argument.
2. **Garland (1973), *p-adic curvature and the cohomology of discrete subgroups of p-adic
   groups*, Ann. of Math. 97.**  This is the combinatorial theorem Layer C formalizes: a spectral
   gap on the links of a building forces `H^i(Γ, ℝ) = 0` for `i` below the rank.  Its hypothesis is
   that `Γ` is a **cocompact** (uniform) lattice in the `p`-adic group; Casselman later removed the
   residue-field size restriction, not the cocompactness one.

The card's route table attributes the *1971 conclusion* to the *1973 method*.  They are different
arguments.

### Why the 1973 method cannot reach `SL_n(𝒪_S)`

An `S`-arithmetic lattice is uniform **iff** the ambient group is anisotropic over the base field.
`SL_n` (`n ≥ 2`) is isotropic over every number field, so `SL_n(𝒪_S)` is a **non-uniform** lattice.
Concretely, on the Bruhat–Tits building of `SL_n(K_v)` the group `SL_n(𝒪_S)` does have finitely many
orbits of cells, but the cell stabilizers are **infinite** — conjugates of `SL_n(𝒪)`.  Garland's
averaging step, and the passage C5 from the complex to the group, both need finite stabilizers.
Without them the descent is the isotropy spectral sequence

```text
E₁^{p,q} = ⊕_{σ ∈ Γ\X_p} H^q(Γ_σ, ℝ)  ⟹  H^{p+q}(Γ, ℝ),
```

whose `q = 1, 2` rows are `H^{1,2}` of the arithmetic stabilizers — exactly the groups the argument
is supposed to kill.  The chain is circular at that point.

There is no rescue by changing `S`: Layer A is free to choose the Dedekind domain, but every ring of
`S`-integers of a number field gives an isotropic group, hence a non-uniform lattice.

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.WeightedGraphSpectralGap

/-!
# Weighted simplicial complexes and the links of their faces

Garland's vanishing method reads a simplicial complex through the links of its faces, each of which
enters only as a weighted graph.  This file supplies that reading: a finite complex presented by its
top-dimensional faces with a weight on each, the induced weight of an arbitrary face, and the link
of a face as a weighted graph.

The link of `σ` joins two vertices *outside* `σ` with the weight of the face they span together with
`σ`; vertices of `σ` itself are isolated in it, which is what makes the weighted degree of a vertex
of the link a multiple of the weight of `σ ∪ {u}` on a pure complex.

* `WeightedComplex` : the complex, presented by weighted top faces.
* `m` : **the weight of a face** — the total weight of the top faces containing it.
* `linkGraph` : **the link of a face, as a weighted graph.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **A finite weighted simplicial complex**, presented by its top-dimensional faces with a
nonnegative weight on each. -/
structure WeightedComplex (V : Type*) [DecidableEq V] where
  /-- the top-dimensional faces -/
  top : Finset (Finset V)
  /-- the weight of a top face -/
  wt : Finset V → ℝ
  /-- weights are nonnegative -/
  wt_nonneg : ∀ s, 0 ≤ wt s

namespace WeightedComplex

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (X : WeightedComplex V)

/-- A finset is a face when it is contained in a top face. -/
def IsFace (τ : Finset V) : Prop := ∃ s ∈ X.top, τ ⊆ s

/-- **The weight of a face**: the total weight of the top faces containing it. -/
noncomputable def m (τ : Finset V) : ℝ := ∑ s ∈ X.top.filter (fun s => τ ⊆ s), X.wt s

theorem m_nonneg (τ : Finset V) : 0 ≤ X.m τ :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun s _ => X.wt_nonneg s

theorem m_mono {τ τ' : Finset V} (h : τ ⊆ τ') : X.m τ' ≤ X.m τ := by
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg ?_ (fun s _ _ => X.wt_nonneg s)
  intro s hs
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hs ⊢
  exact ⟨hs.1, h.trans hs.2⟩

/-- A nonface has zero induced weight. -/
theorem m_eq_zero_of_not_isFace {τ : Finset V} (hτ : ¬ X.IsFace τ) : X.m τ = 0 := by
  unfold m
  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
  intro s hs
  exact False.elim (hτ ⟨s, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hs).1, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hs).2⟩)

/-- The vertices excluded from the link of `σ`: `σ` itself, and the diagonal. -/
private def linkExcluded (σ : Finset V) (u u' : V) : Prop := u = u' ∨ u ∈ σ ∨ u' ∈ σ

instance (σ : Finset V) (u u' : V) : Decidable (linkExcluded σ u u') := by
  unfold linkExcluded; infer_instance

omit [DecidableEq V] in
private theorem linkExcluded_symm {σ : Finset V} {u u' : V} (h : linkExcluded σ u u') :
    linkExcluded σ u' u := by
  rcases h with h | h | h
  exacts [Or.inl h.symm, Or.inr (Or.inr h), Or.inr (Or.inl h)]

/-- **The link of a face, as a weighted graph**: two vertices outside `σ` are joined with the weight
of the face they span together with `σ`. -/
noncomputable def linkGraph (σ : Finset V) : WeightedGraph V where
  w u u' := if linkExcluded σ u u' then 0 else X.m (insert u (insert u' σ))
  w_symm u u' := by
    by_cases h : linkExcluded σ u u'
    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos (linkExcluded_symm h)]
    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hc => h (linkExcluded_symm hc)), Finset.insert_comm]
  w_nonneg u u' := by
    by_cases h : linkExcluded σ u u'
    · rw [if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h]
      exact X.m_nonneg _
  w_diag _ := if_pos (Or.inl rfl)

theorem linkGraph_w_eq_zero (σ : Finset V) {u u' : V} (h : linkExcluded σ u u') :
    (X.linkGraph σ).w u u' = 0 := if_pos h

theorem linkGraph_w_of_not (σ : Finset V) {u u' : V} (h : ¬ linkExcluded σ u u') :
    (X.linkGraph σ).w u u' = X.m (insert u (insert u' σ)) := if_neg h

theorem linkGraph_w_eq (σ : Finset V) (u u' : V) :
    (X.linkGraph σ).w u u'
      = if u = u' ∨ u ∈ σ ∨ u' ∈ σ then 0 else X.m (insert u (insert u' σ)) := rfl

section Pure

theorem insert_insert_subset_iff {σ : Finset V} {u u' : V} {s : Finset V} :
    insert u (insert u' σ) ⊆ s ↔ u ∈ s ∧ u' ∈ s ∧ σ ⊆ s := by
  rw [Finset.insert_subset_iff, Finset.insert_subset_iff]

theorem m_eq_sum_ite (τ : Finset V) :
    X.m τ = ∑ s ∈ X.top, (if τ ⊆ s then X.wt s else 0) := by
  rw [m, Finset.sum_filter]

variable [Fintype V]

/-- **The weighted degree of a vertex of the link of `σ` on a pure complex.**  Every top face
containing `σ ∪ {u}` has exactly `n - |σ|` further vertices, and each of them contributes one edge
of the link at `u`. -/
theorem linkGraph_mass {n : ℕ} (hpure : ∀ s ∈ X.top, s.card = n + 1)
    {σ : Finset V} {u : V} (hu : u ∉ σ) :
    (X.linkGraph σ).mass u = ((n - σ.card : ℕ) : ℝ) * X.m (insert u σ) := by
  classical
  have hw : ∀ u' : V, (X.linkGraph σ).w u u'
      = ∑ s ∈ X.top, (if ((u' ≠ u ∧ u' ∉ σ) ∧ insert u (insert u' σ) ⊆ s) then X.wt s else 0) := by
    intro u'
    by_cases h : linkExcluded σ u u'
    · rw [X.linkGraph_w_eq_zero σ h]
      symm
      refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun s _ => if_neg ?_

import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset

/-!
# The spectral gap of a finite weighted graph

Garland's vanishing method runs on the spectral gap of the links of a simplicial complex, and a link
enters the argument only through its one-skeleton with the weights inherited from the complex.  This
file sets up that one-skeleton: a finite weighted graph, its vertex masses, the mass inner product,
the Dirichlet form, and the statement that a real number is a spectral gap for it.

The gap is carried as a property of a real number rather than as an infimum, because that is the
form Garland's inequality consumes and it needs no compactness.

* `WeightedGraph` : a finite symmetric nonnegative weight with no loops.
* `mass`, `massInner`, `dirichlet` : the vertex masses, the mass inner product, the Dirichlet form.
* `dirichlet_self_eq` : **the Dirichlet form is the mass norm minus the averaging form.**
* `HasSpectralGap`, `spectralGap_apply` : **a spectral gap bounds the deviation from the mass
  average.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **A finite weighted graph**: a symmetric nonnegative weight with no loops. -/
structure WeightedGraph (V : Type*) where
  /-- the weight of an edge -/
  w : V → V → ℝ
  /-- the weight is symmetric -/
  w_symm : ∀ u v, w u v = w v u
  /-- the weight is nonnegative -/
  w_nonneg : ∀ u v, 0 ≤ w u v
  /-- there are no loops -/
  w_diag : ∀ v, w v v = 0

namespace WeightedGraph

/-- Weighted graphs are determined by their edge-weight function. -/
@[ext] theorem ext {V : Type*} {G H : WeightedGraph V}
    (h : ∀ u v, G.w u v = H.w u v) : G = H := by
  cases G with
  | mk gw gsym gnon gdiag =>
    cases H with
    | mk hw hsym hnon hdiag =>
      have hwh : gw = hw := funext fun u => funext fun v => h u v
      subst hw
      rfl

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : WeightedGraph V)

/-- The mass of a vertex: the total weight of the edges at it. -/
def mass (v : V) : ℝ := ∑ u, G.w v u

theorem mass_nonneg (v : V) : 0 ≤ G.mass v :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun u _ => G.w_nonneg v u

/-- The total mass of the graph. -/
def totalMass : ℝ := ∑ v, G.mass v

theorem totalMass_nonneg : 0 ≤ G.totalMass :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun v _ => G.mass_nonneg v

/-- The inner product on functions weighted by the vertex masses. -/
def massInner (f g : V → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ v, G.mass v * (f v * g v)

theorem massInner_self_nonneg (f : V → ℝ) : 0 ≤ G.massInner f f :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun v _ => mul_nonneg (G.mass_nonneg v) (mul_self_nonneg _)

/-- The Dirichlet form of the graph. -/
noncomputable def dirichlet (f g : V → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * ((f v - f u) * (g v - g u))) / 2

theorem dirichlet_self_nonneg (f : V → ℝ) : 0 ≤ G.dirichlet f f := by
  refine div_nonneg (Finset.sum_nonneg fun v _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun u _ => ?_) (by norm_num)
  exact mul_nonneg (G.w_nonneg v u) (mul_self_nonneg _)

theorem dirichlet_sub_const (f : V → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
    G.dirichlet (fun v => f v - c) (fun v => f v - c) = G.dirichlet f f := by
  refine congrArg (· / 2) (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun u _ => ?_)
  ring_nf

theorem sum_sum_w_mul_left (h : V → ℝ) :
    (∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * h v) = ∑ v, G.mass v * h v :=
  Finset.sum_congr rfl fun _ _ => (Finset.sum_mul _ _ _).symm

theorem sum_sum_w_mul_right (h : V → ℝ) :
    (∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * h u) = ∑ v, G.mass v * h v := by
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun u _ => ?_
  rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
  exact congrArg (· * h u) (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => G.w_symm v u)

/-- **The Dirichlet form as mass norm minus averaging.** -/
theorem dirichlet_self_eq (f : V → ℝ) :
    G.dirichlet f f = G.massInner f f - ∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * (f v * f u) := by
  have h1 : (∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * ((f v - f u) * (f v - f u)))
      = (∑ v, ∑ u, (G.w v u * (f v * f v) + G.w v u * (f u * f u)
          - 2 * (G.w v u * (f v * f u)))) :=
    Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun u _ => by ring
  have h2 : ∀ F₁ F₂ F₃ : V → V → ℝ,
      (∑ v, ∑ u, (F₁ v u + F₂ v u - 2 * F₃ v u))
        = (∑ v, ∑ u, F₁ v u) + (∑ v, ∑ u, F₂ v u) - 2 * ∑ v, ∑ u, F₃ v u := by
    intro F₁ F₂ F₃
    simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [dirichlet, h1, h2, G.sum_sum_w_mul_left (fun v => f v * f v),
    G.sum_sum_w_mul_right (fun v => f v * f v)]
  show (G.massInner f f + G.massInner f f - 2 * ∑ v, ∑ u, G.w v u * (f v * f u)) / 2 = _
  ring

/-- The mass average of a function. -/
noncomputable def mean (f : V → ℝ) : ℝ := (∑ v, G.mass v * f v) / G.totalMass

theorem sum_mass_sub_mean (f : V → ℝ) (htot : G.totalMass ≠ 0) :
    (∑ v, G.mass v * (f v - G.mean f)) = 0 := by
  have h : (∑ v, G.mass v * (f v - G.mean f))
      = (∑ v, G.mass v * f v) - G.mean f * G.totalMass := by
    rw [totalMass, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => by ring

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RieszMellinPair

/-!
# The Riesz mean as a logarithmic average of partial sums

The second-order Riesz mean carries the weight `log(N/n)`.  Telescoping that weight,

```text
log N - log n = ∑_{m=n}^{N-1} ( log(m+1) - log m ) ,
```

and exchanging the two finite sums turns the weighted sum of coefficients into a weighted sum of
*partial* sums:

```text
∑_{n < N} aₙ ( log N - log(n+1) ) = ∑_{m < N} ( log(m+1) - log m ) · ∑_{n < m} aₙ .
```

The weights are nonnegative and add up to `log N`, so a uniform bound on the partial sums transfers
to the Riesz mean with the factor `log N`.  This is the discrete half of the Riesz-mean method,
requiring no contour integral; the analytic half is the kernel `1/w²` and its Mellin pair.
-/

noncomputable section

open Finset

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-- The logarithmic increments telescope to `log N`. -/
theorem sum_log_increment (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N, (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) = Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  have h : ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N, (Real.log ((m : ℕ) + 1 : ℕ) - Real.log ((m : ℕ) : ℕ))
      = Real.log ((N : ℕ) : ℝ) - Real.log ((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    Finset.sum_range_sub (fun m : ℕ => Real.log ((m : ℕ) : ℝ)) N
  simpa using h

/-- Each logarithmic increment is nonnegative. -/
theorem log_increment_nonneg (m : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with hm | hm
  · subst hm
    simp
  · have hm0 : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
    have : Real.log (m : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) :=
      Real.log_le_log hm0 (by linarith)
    linarith

/-- **The Riesz mean is a logarithmic average of the partial sums.** -/
theorem rieszLogSum_eq_sum_partialSum (a : ℕ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
      = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N,
          ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
            * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n) := by
  induction N with
  | zero => simp
  | succ N ih =>
    have hsplit : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
          a n * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
        = (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,
            a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ)))
          + ((Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ))
            * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
      have hlast : a N * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
          - (Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ)) = 0 := by
        have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
        rw [hcast]
        ring
      have hterm : ∀ n ∈ Finset.range N,
          a n * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
            = a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
              + ((Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ)) * a n := by
        intro n _
        have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
        rw [hcast]
        ring
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
      have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
      rw [hcast] at hlast ⊢
      rw [hlast, add_zero]
    rw [hsplit, ih, Finset.sum_range_succ]

/-- **A uniform bound on the partial sums bounds the Riesz mean by `log N` times that bound.** -/
theorem norm_rieszLogSum_le {a : ℕ → ℂ} {B : ℝ} {N : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range N, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n‖ ≤ B) :
    ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))‖
      ≤ B * Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  rw [rieszLogSum_eq_sum_partialSum]
  refine le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _) ?_
  have hterm : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range N,
      ‖((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
        * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n)‖
        ≤ B * (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) := by
    intro m hm
    have hw : ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
        = ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
      push_cast
      ring
    rw [hw, norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonneg (log_increment_nonneg m)]
    calc (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) * ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n‖
        ≤ (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) * B :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h m hm) (log_increment_nonneg m)
      _ = B * (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) := by ring
  refine le_trans (Finset.sum_le_sum hterm) ?_
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, sum_log_increment]

/-!
# Polynomial moments of literal coprime deletion polygons

For actual moduli `P=p+1` and `Q=q+1`, join the successive prefix endpoints
`(n mod P,n mod Q)` by straight segments. Their velocities are exactly the existing
Euler-deletion coefficients, and one common period is a closed polygon.

CRT factors every polynomial segment density into two explicit one-coordinate phase sums.
All coefficient-degree-at-most-three polynomial one-forms have zero circulation. The
higher moment `integral x*y^3 dx` is exactly `P*(P-1)*Q*(Q-1)*(Q-2)/120` for coprime
`P,Q`. In particular the literal moduli-2-and-3 path gives the closed value `1/10`.

This is a finite unweighted arithmetic statement. It supplies no assertion about a weighted
infinite product, no vanishing at a zeta zero, and no RH implication. Polynomial-moment
and path-signature methods have published ancestry; no global novelty claim is made here.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
namespace RHTower.DeletionJointPolygon
noncomputable section

/-- Velocity of the literal modulus `p+1` deletion path. -/
def velocity (p n : ℕ) : ℝ := blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1)

/-- Straight interpolation of the exact residue-valued prefix. -/
def position (p n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := (n % (p+1) : ℕ) + t * velocity p n

/-- Polynomial one-form integrated along one full common period. -/
def circulation (p q a b : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range ((p+1)*(q+1)),
    position p n t ^ a * position q n t ^ b * velocity p n

/-- Position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def phaseMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) + ((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

/-- Velocity-weighted position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def velocityMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) - (p:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

theorem velocity_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) : velocity p n = 1 := by
  have hd : ¬ p+1 ∣ n+1 := Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt (Nat.succ_pos n)
    (Nat.succ_lt_succ hn)
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient, hd]

theorem velocity_last (p : ℕ) : velocity p p = -(p:ℝ) := by
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient]

theorem position_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) (t : ℝ) :
    position p n t = (n:ℝ)+t := by
  simp [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hn), velocity_of_lt hn]

theorem position_last (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : position p p t = (p:ℝ)*(1-t) := by
  simp only [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_self p), velocity_last]
  ring

theorem velocity_periodic (p : ℕ) : Function.Periodic (velocity p) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  exact congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ))
    (DeletionCoprimeWords.shifted_deletion_periodic (p+1) n)

theorem position_periodic (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    Function.Periodic (fun n => position p n t) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  simp only [position, Nat.add_mod_right, velocity_periodic p n]

theorem sum_position_pow (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k) = phaseMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last]
  unfold phaseMoment
  congr 1
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun n hn => by rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn)])

theorem sum_position_pow_velocity (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      velocityMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last, velocity_last]
  unfold velocityMoment
  have hs : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, ((n:ℝ)+t)^k := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n hn
    rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), velocity_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), mul_one]
  rw [hs]
  ring

/-- The starting coordinate is the actual sum of previous deletion jumps. -/
theorem position_zero_eq_prefix (p n : ℕ) :
    position p n 0 = (deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n : ℝ) := by
  simp only [position, zero_mul, add_zero, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, Int.cast_natCast]

/-- Consecutive straight segments meet at their endpoints. -/
theorem segment_endpoint (p n : ℕ) : position p n 1 = position p (n+1) 0 := by
  have h : deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n + blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1) =
      deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) (n+1) := by
    exact (Finset.sum_range_succ _ _).symm
  rw [deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod] at h
  have hr := congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ)) h
  simpa only [position, velocity, one_mul, zero_mul, add_zero, Int.cast_add, Int.cast_natCast] using hr

/-- A common period returns both literal coordinates to the origin. -/
theorem common_period_closed (p q : ℕ) :
    position p ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 ∧ position q ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 := by
  simp [position]

/-- CRT factors the actual segment integrand; no averaging approximation is used. -/

/-!
# Hardy-fiber deletion as vertical growth of an entire canonical product

Removing one complete Xi fiber from the genus-one relative resolvent is exactly the logarithmic
derivative of `xiCanonicalProductAway`.  The genus-one normalization is essential: its elementary
factor supplies the constant subtraction at the functional-equation centre.

For a Hardy critical fiber, RH is therefore equivalent to nonnegative vertical logarithmic-modulus
velocity of this one entire deflated product only in the positive high-frequency strip
`4 < Re z`, `0 < Im z < 1/2`.  Central and negative frequencies require no hypothesis.
-/

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- A point off the Xi divisor is also off the divisor of every fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem xiCanonicalProductAway_ne_zero_of_XiC_ne_zero
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    xiCanonicalProductAway ρ z ≠ 0 := by
  have hcan : xiCanonicalProduct z ≠ 0 := by
    intro hzero
    apply hz
    have hfactor := congrFun xiHadamardQuotient_mul_canonicalProduct z
    rw [Pi.mul_apply] at hfactor
    rw [← hfactor, hzero, mul_zero]
  intro haway
  apply hcan
  rw [xiCanonicalProduct_factorization_at_support ρ z, haway, mul_zero]

/-- Exact genus-one deletion identity: the logarithmic derivative of the entire product with the
`ρ` fiber removed is the full relative resolvent trace minus that complete finite fiber. -/
theorem logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z =
      xiRelativeResolventTrace z -
        ∑ q ∈ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q := by
  have hzaway : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, z ≠ xiSpectralPoint q.1 := by
    intro q hq
    apply hz
    rw [hq]
    exact XiC_xiSpectralPoint_eq_zero q.1
  have hlog := logDeriv_canonicalProductE1Indexed
    (a := fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)
    (fun q => xiSpectralPoint_ne_zero q.1)
    (xiCanonicalProductAway_inv_sq_summable ρ) hzaway
  have hterm : ∀ q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ,
      ((z - xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹ + (xiSpectralPoint q.1)⁻¹) =
        xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 := by
    intro q
    rw [xiRelativeResolventTerm]
    rw [show z - xiSpectralPoint q.1 =
      -(xiSpectralPoint q.1 - z) by ring, inv_neg]
    ring
  have hsum : Summable (xiRelativeResolventTerm z) :=
    summable_xiRelativeResolventTerm hz
  have hsplit := hsum.sum_add_tsum_subtype_compl (xiZeroCopyFiber ρ)
  let e : XiZeroCopyAway ρ ≃
      {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} :=
    { toFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      invFun := fun q =>
        ⟨q.1, by simpa only [mem_xiZeroCopyFiber] using q.2⟩
      left_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl
      right_inv := fun q => by cases q; rfl }
  have haway_tsum :=
    e.tsum_eq (fun q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ} =>
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1)
  change (∑' q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ, xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1) =
    ∑' q : {q : XiZeroCopy // q ∉ xiZeroCopyFiber ρ},
      xiRelativeResolventTerm z q.1 at haway_tsum
  change logDeriv
    (canonicalProductE1Indexed
      (fun q : XiZeroCopyAway ρ => xiSpectralPoint q.1)) z = _
  rw [hlog]
  simp_rw [hterm]
  rw [haway_tsum, xiRelativeResolventTrace, ← hsplit]
  ring

/-- On the continued prime--Gamma comparison domain, the fixed-fiber-deflated source trace is
literally the logarithmic derivative of the entire fiber-deleted canonical product. -/
theorem ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway
    (ρ : XiDivisorSupport) {z : ℂ}
    (hspos : 0 < (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I).re)
    (hs1 : 1 / 2 + z * Complex.I ≠ 1)
    (hzeta : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + z * Complex.I) ≠ 0) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace ρ z =
      logDeriv (xiCanonicalProductAway ρ) z := by
  have hXi : XiC z ≠ 0 :=
    XiC_ne_zero_of_continuedPrimeArch_domain hspos hs1 hzeta
  rw [ccmFixedFiberDeflatedRelativeTrace_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hspos hs1 hzeta,
    ← logDeriv_xiCanonicalProductAway_eq_xiTrace_sub_fiber ρ hXi]

/-- On a critical fiber, fixed-fiber deflation is exactly subtraction of a multiplicity-weighted
rank-one Nevanlinna--Pick kernel.  This identifies genus-one divisor deletion with the
Schur-complement chart used by Pick and de Branges methods. -/
theorem ccmFixedCriticalFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel_eq_sub_pickKernel

    (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0)
    (hzw : z ≠ (starRingEnd ℂ) w) :
    ccmFixedFiberDeflatedCauchyKernel ρ z w =
      ccmContinuedCauchyKernel z w -

def differentialIndependentObservableNetOrderEmbedding

/-!
## Asymptotic clock translation length

Differential order on a group of reversible substitutions is a nonnegative subadditive cost:
composition can expose at most the sum of the two input jet orders.  The following abstract kernel
isolates the consequence needed by the differential-birational clock theory.  Fekete's lemma gives
an actual asymptotic speed, and bounded coordinate changes disappear after normalization.  Thus
the speed is invariant under differential-birational conjugacy once the concrete differential-order
cost has been supplied.
-/

/-- A nonnegative subadditive cost on a group of reversible clock changes. -/
structure SubadditiveClockGauge (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  cost : G → ℝ
  cost_nonneg : ∀ g, 0 ≤ cost g
  cost_one : cost 1 = 0
  cost_mul_le : ∀ g h, cost (g * h) ≤ cost g + cost h

namespace SubadditiveClockGauge

open Filter Topology

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] (W : SubadditiveClockGauge G)

/-- Cost of the `n`-fold reversible clock change. -/
def orbitCost (g : G) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := W.cost (g ^ n)

/-- Iterated clock cost is a subadditive sequence. -/
theorem orbitCost_subadditive (g : G) : Subadditive (W.orbitCost g) := by
  intro m n
  rw [orbitCost, orbitCost, orbitCost, pow_add]
  exact W.cost_mul_le _ _

theorem normalizedOrbitCost_bddBelow (g : G) :
    BddBelow (Set.range fun n ↦ W.orbitCost g n / n) := by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  rintro y ⟨n, rfl⟩
  exact div_nonneg (W.cost_nonneg _) (Nat.cast_nonneg n)

/-- The asymptotic clock translation length. -/
noncomputable def translationLength (g : G) : ℝ :=
  (W.orbitCost_subadditive g).lim

/-- Fekete's lemma: normalized clock cost has an actual limit, not merely a limsup. -/
theorem tendsto_normalizedOrbitCost (g : G) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ W.orbitCost g n / n) atTop
      (nhds (W.translationLength g)) := by
  exact (W.orbitCost_subadditive g).tendsto_lim
    (W.normalizedOrbitCost_bddBelow g)

/-- Conjugation is a change of reversible clock coordinates. -/
def conjugate (h g : G) : G := h * g * h⁻¹

@[simp] theorem conjugate_pow (h g : G) (n : ℕ) :
    (conjugate h g) ^ n = h * g ^ n * h⁻¹ := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [conjugate]
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [pow_succ, ih, pow_succ]
      simp [conjugate, mul_assoc]

/-- A coordinate change alters every finite iterate cost by at most a fixed additive amount. -/
theorem orbitCost_conjugate_le (h g : G) (n : ℕ) :
    W.orbitCost (conjugate h g) n ≤
      W.orbitCost g n + (W.cost h + W.cost h⁻¹) := by
  rw [orbitCost, conjugate_pow]
  calc
    W.cost (h * g ^ n * h⁻¹) ≤ W.cost (h * g ^ n) + W.cost h⁻¹ :=
      W.cost_mul_le _ _
    _ ≤ (W.cost h + W.cost (g ^ n)) + W.cost h⁻¹ := by
      linarith [W.cost_mul_le h (g ^ n)]
    _ = W.orbitCost g n + (W.cost h + W.cost h⁻¹) := by
      rw [orbitCost]
      ring

theorem orbitCost_le_conjugate (h g : G) (n : ℕ) :
    W.orbitCost g n ≤
      W.orbitCost (conjugate h g) n + (W.cost h + W.cost h⁻¹) := by
  have hconj : conjugate h⁻¹ (conjugate h g) = g := by
    simp [conjugate, mul_assoc]
  have hle := W.orbitCost_conjugate_le h⁻¹ (conjugate h g) n
  rw [hconj] at hle
  simpa [add_comm] using hle

/-- **Coordinate-invariant clock speed.**  Every fixed reversible change of differential
coordinates contributes only a bounded finite-order overhead, so it does not alter asymptotic
translation length. -/
theorem translationLength_conjugate (h g : G) :
    W.translationLength (conjugate h g) = W.translationLength g := by
  let B : ℝ := W.cost h + W.cost h⁻¹
  have hB : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ B / n) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    tendsto_const_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat B
  have hg := W.tendsto_normalizedOrbitCost g
  have hlower : Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ W.orbitCost g n / n - B / n) atTop
      (nhds (W.translationLength g)) := by
    simpa using hg.sub hB
  have hupper : Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ W.orbitCost g n / n + B / n) atTop
      (nhds (W.translationLength g)) := by
    simpa using hg.add hB
  have hsandwich : Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ W.orbitCost (conjugate h g) n / n) atTop
      (nhds (W.translationLength g)) := by

abs_freeDifferentialOrder_conjugate_sub_le
    (h σ : FreeAut (C := C) (ι := ι)) :
    abs ((freeDifferentialOrder (SubadditiveClockGauge.conjugate h σ) : ℝ) -
      freeDifferentialOrder σ) ≤
        ((freeDifferentialOrder h + freeDifferentialOrder h⁻¹ : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor
  · have hle := freeDifferentialOrder_le_conjugate h σ
    have hleR : (freeDifferentialOrder σ : ℝ) ≤
        freeDifferentialOrder (SubadditiveClockGauge.conjugate h σ) +
          (freeDifferentialOrder h + freeDifferentialOrder h⁻¹) := by
      exact_mod_cast hle
    push_cast at hleR ⊢
    linarith
  · have hle := freeDifferentialOrder_conjugate_le h σ
    have hleR :
        (freeDifferentialOrder (SubadditiveClockGauge.conjugate h σ) : ℝ) ≤
          freeDifferentialOrder σ +
            (freeDifferentialOrder h + freeDifferentialOrder h⁻¹) := by
      exact_mod_cast hle
    push_cast at hleR ⊢
    linarith

def freeOrderGauge : SubadditiveClockGauge (FreeAut (C := C) (ι := ι)) where
  cost σ := freeDifferentialOrder σ
  cost_nonneg σ := Nat.cast_nonneg _
  cost_one := by simp
  cost_mul_le σ τ := by exact_mod_cast freeDifferentialOrder_mul_le σ τ

theorem freeOrderGauge_orbitCost (σ : FreeAut (C := C) (ι := ι)) (n : ℕ) :
    freeOrderGauge.orbitCost σ n = freeDifferentialOrder (σ ^ n) := rfl

theorem tendsto_normalized_freeDifferentialOrder
    (σ : FreeAut (C := C) (ι := ι)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (freeDifferentialOrder (σ ^ n) : ℝ) / n)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (freeOrderGauge.translationLength σ)) := by
  simpa [freeOrderGauge_orbitCost] using freeOrderGauge.tendsto_normalizedOrbitCost σ

/-- Intrinsic clock speed is invariant under every differential-birational coordinate change. -/
theorem freeOrderTranslationLength_conjugate
    (h σ : FreeAut (C := C) (ι := ι)) :
    freeOrderGauge.translationLength (SubadditiveClockGauge.conjugate h σ) =
      freeOrderGauge.translationLength σ :=
  freeOrderGauge.translationLength_conjugate h σ

end

/-- A gamma matrix carries right-handed Weyl components to left-handed ones. -/
theorem hlsWeyl_leftProjector_gamma (μ : Fin 4) :
    hlsWeylLeftProjector * hlsWeylGamma μ = hlsWeylGamma μ * hlsWeylRightProjector := by
  simp [hlsWeylLeftProjector, hlsWeylRightProjector, hlsWeylGamma,
    Matrix.fromBlocks_multiply]

/-- A gamma matrix carries left-handed Weyl components to right-handed ones. -/
theorem hlsWeyl_rightProjector_gamma (μ : Fin 4) :
    hlsWeylRightProjector * hlsWeylGamma μ = hlsWeylGamma μ * hlsWeylLeftProjector := by
  simp [hlsWeylLeftProjector, hlsWeylRightProjector, hlsWeylGamma,
    Matrix.fromBlocks_multiply]

/-- Weyl-spinor transformation and translation-invariance laws on a common invariant domain.
The matrices `lorentzOnSpinor` are supplied representation data; deriving the unique Weyl form
from physical hypotheses is part of the unformalized HLS classification proof. -/
structure HLSWeylSuperchargeData (E : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] where
  commonDomain : Submodule ℂ E
  translation : Fin 4 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  lorentz : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  supercharge : Fin 2 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  lorentzOnSpinor : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ
  translation_commutes_supercharge : ∀ μ α,
    hlsDomainCommutator commonDomain (translation μ) (supercharge α) = 0
  lorentz_covariant_supercharge : ∀ μ ν α,
    hlsDomainCommutator commonDomain (lorentz μ ν) (supercharge α) =
      ∑ β, (lorentzOnSpinor μ ν α β) • supercharge β

/-- Full common-domain Weyl superalgebra interface.  It records the mixed anticommutator,
same-chirality central charge, centrality, and positivity used in the HLS classification.  It
does not derive them: that derivation is precisely the remaining physical HLS theorem. -/
structure HLSWeylSuperalgebraData (N : Type v) [DecidableEq N] (E : Type u)
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] where
  commonDomain : Submodule ℂ E
  translation : Fin 4 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  supercharge : N → Fin 2 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  conjugateSupercharge : N → Fin 2 → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  sigma : Fin 4 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ
  centralCharge : N → N → commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ] commonDomain
  conjugate_adjoint : ∀ I α (ψ φ : commonDomain),
    inner ℂ (supercharge I α ψ : E) (φ : E) =
      inner ℂ (ψ : E) (conjugateSupercharge I α φ : E)
  mixed_anticommutator : ∀ I J α β,
    hlsDomainAnticommutator commonDomain (supercharge I α) (conjugateSupercharge J β) =
      ∑ μ, (if I = J then (2 : ℂ) * sigma μ α β else 0) • translation μ
  same_chirality_anticommutator : ∀ I J α β,
    hlsDomainAnticommutator commonDomain (supercharge I α) (supercharge J β) =
      hlsWeylEpsilon α β • centralCharge I J
  centralCharge_antisymmetric : ∀ I J, centralCharge I J = -centralCharge J I
  central_commutes_translation : ∀ I J μ,
    hlsDomainCommutator commonDomain (centralCharge I J) (translation μ) = 0
  central_commutes_supercharge : ∀ I J K α,
    hlsDomainCommutator commonDomain (centralCharge I J) (supercharge K α) = 0
  mixed_positive : ∀ I α (ψ : commonDomain),
    0 ≤ (inner ℂ
      ((hlsDomainAnticommutator commonDomain (supercharge I α)
        (conjugateSupercharge I α) ψ : commonDomain) : E)
      (ψ : E)).re

/-- A full Weyl superalgebra on the same common domain as genuine Poincaré generators.  Unlike
the reusable algebra interface above, this record identifies its translations and Lorentz action
with the self-adjoint Poincaré system, so every HLS bracket is an equation among one set of
physical operators. -/
structure HLSPoincareWeylSuperalgebraData (N : Type v) [DecidableEq N] (E : Type u)
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] where
  poincare : HLSInfinitesimalPoincareLieData E
  supercharge : N → Fin 2 → poincare.generators.commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ]
    poincare.generators.commonDomain
  conjugateSupercharge : N → Fin 2 → poincare.generators.commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ]
    poincare.generators.commonDomain
  lorentzOnSpinor : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ
  lorentzOnSpinor_antisymmetric : ∀ μ ν,
    lorentzOnSpinor μ ν = -lorentzOnSpinor ν μ
  lorentzOnSpinor_bracket : ∀ μ ν ρ σ,
    hlsMatrixCommutator (lorentzOnSpinor μ ν) (lorentzOnSpinor ρ σ) =
      Complex.I •
        (hlsComplexMinkowskiMetric μ σ • lorentzOnSpinor ν ρ +
          hlsComplexMinkowskiMetric ν ρ • lorentzOnSpinor μ σ -
          hlsComplexMinkowskiMetric μ ρ • lorentzOnSpinor ν σ -
          hlsComplexMinkowskiMetric ν σ • lorentzOnSpinor μ ρ)
  sigma : Fin 4 → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ
  sigma_standard : sigma = hlsWeylSigma
  centralCharge : N → N → poincare.generators.commonDomain →ₗ[ℂ]
    poincare.generators.commonDomain

/-!
# Cyclic projective normal-form classification

This leaf refines the scaling-or-translation projective normal form by separating the scaling
case into nontrivial finite cyclic and infinite-order branches.  It is the purely projective
four-branch parent of the scalar persistent-gauge classification.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- Every coefficient-fixing rational-function automorphism over an algebraically closed field is
either the identity, conjugate to a nontrivial finite-order scaling, conjugate to an infinite-order
scaling, or conjugate to unit translation. -/
theorem ratFuncAlgEquiv_cyclicNormalForm
    [IsAlgClosed K] (e : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K) :
    e = AlgEquiv.refl ∨
      (∃ (h : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K) (u : Kˣ) (N : ℕ),
        2 ≤ N ∧ orderOf u = N ∧
          h.symm * e * h = ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv u) ∨
      (∃ (h : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K) (u : Kˣ),
        orderOf u = 0 ∧
          h.symm * e * h = ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv u) ∨
      (∃ h : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K,
        h.symm * e * h = ratFuncTranslationEquiv 1) := by
  by_cases he : e = AlgEquiv.refl
  · exact Or.inl he
  · right
    rcases ratFuncAlgEquiv_normalForm e he with hscale | htranslation
    · obtain ⟨h, u, hu⟩ := hscale
      have huOne : u ≠ 1 := by
        intro hu1
        apply he
        calc
          e = h * (h.symm * e * h) * h.symm := by
            change e = h * (h⁻¹ * e * h) * h⁻¹
            group
          _ = h * ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv u * h.symm := by rw [hu]
          _ = h * AlgEquiv.refl * h.symm := by
            rw [hu1, ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv_one]
          _ = AlgEquiv.refl := by
            change h * 1 * h⁻¹ = 1
            group
      by_cases horder : orderOf u = 0
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨h, u, horder, hu⟩)
      · left
        have horderOne : orderOf u ≠ 1 := by
          intro h
          exact huOne (orderOf_eq_one_iff.mp h)
        refine ⟨h, u, orderOf u, ?_, rfl, hu⟩
        have hpos : 0 < orderOf u := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero horder
        omega
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr htranslation)

end

/-!
# Affine normal forms on a rational coordinate

This module closes the affine part of the projective cyclic-normal-form argument.  An affine
automorphism `X ↦ uX + b` is either the identity, conjugate to its scalar linear part when
`u ≠ 1`, or conjugate to unit translation when `u = 1` and `b ≠ 0`.

The statements are literal equalities of coefficient-fixing automorphisms of `K(X)`.  They do
not assume a normal-form or fixed-field conclusion as input.
-/

open Polynomial

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- Two coefficient-fixing endomorphisms of `K(X)` agree when they agree on `X`. -/
private theorem ratFuncAlgHom_ext_X
    {f g : RatFunc K →ₐ[K] RatFunc K}
    (hX : f RatFunc.X = g RatFunc.X) :
    f = g := by
  apply AlgHom.ext
  intro z
  have hring : f.toRingHom = g.toRingHom := by
    apply IsFractionRing.ringHom_ext (A := K[X])
    intro p
    have hpoly :
        f.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) =
          g.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) := by
      apply Polynomial.ringHom_ext
      · intro c
        change f (algebraMap K (RatFunc K) c) =
          g (algebraMap K (RatFunc K) c)
        rw [f.commutes, g.commutes]
      · simpa [RatFunc.algebraMap_X] using hX
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun hpoly p
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hring z

/-- Two coefficient-fixing automorphisms of `K(X)` agree when they agree on `X`. -/
private theorem ratFuncAlgEquiv_ext_X
    {f g : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K}
    (hX : f RatFunc.X = g RatFunc.X) :
    f = g := by
  have hhom : f.toAlgHom = g.toAlgHom :=
    ratFuncAlgHom_ext_X hX
  apply AlgEquiv.ext
  intro z
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun hhom z

/-- The affine automorphism `X ↦ uX + b` of `K(X)`. -/
def ratFuncAffineEquiv (u : Kˣ) (b : K) : RatFunc K ≃ₐ[K] RatFunc K :=
  ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv u * ratFuncTranslationEquiv b

theorem ratFuncAffineEquiv_X (u : Kˣ) (b : K) :
    ratFuncAffineEquiv u b RatFunc.X =
      algebraMap K (RatFunc K) (u : K) * RatFunc.X +
        algebraMap K (RatFunc K) b := by
  change ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv u
      (ratFuncTranslationEquiv b RatFunc.X) = _
  rw [ratFuncTranslationEquiv_X, map_add,
    ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv_X, AlgEquiv.commutes]

  rw [ratFuncAffineEquiv, ratFuncUnitScaleEquiv_one,
    ratFuncTranslationEquiv_zero]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem solvesWaveEq_comp_timeReflect (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u₁) (h : SolvesWaveEq u₁ V) :
    SolvesWaveEq (fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) (fun q => V (timeReflect d q))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem solvesWaveEq_comp_timeReflect (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u₁) (h : SolvesWaveEq u₁ V) :
    SolvesWaveEq (fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) (fun q => V (timeReflect d q))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  intro p
  have hsecond : waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) p
      = waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁) (timeReflect d p) := by
    have hfirst : (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q))
        = fun q => -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁ (timeReflect d q) := by
      funext q
      exact waveDirDeriv_timeDir_comp_timeReflect hu q
    rw [hfirst]
    have hneg : (fun q : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) => -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁ (timeReflect d q))
        = fun q => (fun r => -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁ r) (timeReflect d q) := rfl
    rw [hneg, waveDirDeriv_comp_timeReflect ((contDiff_dirDeriv hu _).neg), timeReflect_timeDir,
      waveDirDeriv_neg_dir]
    have hnegfun : waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (fun r : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) =>
        -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁ r) (timeReflect d p)
        = -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁) (timeReflect d p) := by
      have hfd : HasFDerivAt (fun r : ℝ × (Fin d → ℝ) => -waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁ r)
          (-(fderiv ℝ (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) u₁) (timeReflect d p))) (timeReflect d p) :=
        (differentiableAt_of_contDiff_infty' (contDiff_dirDeriv hu _)
          (timeReflect d p)).hasFDerivAt.neg
      rw [waveDirDeriv, waveDirDeriv, hfd.fderiv]
      rfl
    rw [hnegfun, neg_neg]
  have hspace : ∀ i : Fin d,
      waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) p
        = waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u₁) (timeReflect d p) := by
    intro i
    have hfirst : (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q))
        = fun q => waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) u₁ (timeReflect d q) := by
      funext q
      exact waveDirDeriv_spaceDir_comp_timeReflect hu i q
    rw [hfirst]
    exact waveDirDeriv_spaceDir_comp_timeReflect (contDiff_dirDeriv hu _) i p
  show waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) (waveDirDeriv (timeDir d) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) p
    = (∑ i : Fin d, waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i)
        (waveDirDeriv (spaceDir d i) fun q => u₁ (timeReflect d q)) p)
      + V (timeReflect d p) * u₁ (timeReflect d p)
  rw [hsecond, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hspace i]
  exact h (timeReflect d p)

expansion gives
\[
 \frac{|S_N(\rho)|}{|S_N(\rho^\dagger)|}

\tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, the raw source decay rates are \(\beta\) and \(1-\beta\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\rho=\frac12
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{the reflected raw tail rates agree}.
\tag{2}

For the normalized coherence, the zero rate is \(N^{-1}\) on both fibres; the useful reflected
quantity is instead the free-energy spike contrast:
\[

finite-factor-invariant reader is therefore a narrow target. A skeptical referee can reasonably
ask which active RH program actually asserts all three hypotheses. Without a named natural
construction forced into that category, the theorem is a structural warning rather than a
decisive route closure.

The trilemma says that a successful method must retain weighted-tail information, react to finite
factors, or be discontinuous. This is logically complete, but it does not supply or control a
surviving RH detector. The paper answers its local question while leaving the main source-side
positivity problem unchanged.

The manuscript appropriately disclaims novelty for Hankel reformulations. Coupling an
RH-equivalent criterion to a dense local orbit proves incompatibility with one classifier class;
it does not move the criterion's missing sign estimate closer to proof.

The strongest revision would pair the local collapse with an explicit global escape theorem:
one source-defined weighted-tail observable that lies outside the collapsed topology, reconstructs
the complete off-critical divisor, and quantitatively classifies every false-RH configuration.

# FZZ-P covariant reporter conservation rigidity

- **ID:** FZZ-P-HC8
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM / unique moving-reporter classification and selection no-go
- **Source:** HC6 exact flow + HC7 full coefficient-space action
- **Lean:** `GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.FZZCigarParityCovariantReporterConservationRigidity`
- **Statement:** A unique source-covariant moving Hermitian reporter exactly conserves unit diagonal
  energy, but it conserves the complete reflected mismatch and therefore cannot produce matching.

## Main theorem

For the HC6 stabilized flow, write

`e=exp(Pt)`, `k=(Q/R)(e-1)`

and

`q=k/e=(Q/R)(1-exp(-Pt))`.

The moving Hermitian reporter

`C_t=(q^2,q,0,1)`

satisfies, for every real time and state,

`H_(C_t)(Phi_t u)=H_(0,0,0,1)(u)`.

At coefficient level this reporter is unique: the pullback equations

`A'=0`, `B'=0`, `C'=0`, `d'=1`

hold exactly when `(a,b,c,d)=(q^2,q,0,1)`.

For every centered Mellin carrier and every time,

`H_(C_t)(Phi_t M(rho))=H_(C_t)(Phi_t M(reflect rho)) <-> Re rho=1/2`.

More strongly, the whole reflected reading difference is independent of time and equals the
initial unit-diagonal reflected defect.  Thus every off-wall carrier remains unmatched at every
time.  Universal covariant matching on all open-strip parity-Mellin modes at any chosen scale and
time is equivalent to RH.

## Paper proof

HC7 gives the pulled coefficients

`(e^2 a-2 e k b+k^2 d, e b-k d, e c, d)`.

Substitution of `(q^2,q,0,1)` with `q=k/e` reduces these to `(0,0,0,1)`, proving conservation.
Conversely, `d=1`; since `e>0`, `ec=0` forces `c=0`; then `eb-kd=0` forces `b=k/e=q`; finally the
first equation forces `a=q^2`.  This proves uniqueness without any zero or target input.

Apply conservation first to `M(rho)` and then to `M(reflect rho)`.  HC5's unit-diagonal detector
theorem yields the critical-line equivalence.  Subtracting the two identities proves exact defect
conservation.  Quantifying matching over source-defined parity-Mellin modes converts the moving
predicate to HC3's unit-diagonal matching predicate, already proved equivalent to RH.

## New route knowledge

- fixed all-time reporters fail, but a unique contragredient moving reporter exists;
- its coefficients are source-only and explicit at every real time;
- moving compensation removes HC6/HC7 cone escape at pullback level;
- conservation retains the detector but preserves every off-wall mismatch exactly;
- covariant transport is therefore kinematic, not dissipative or selective;
- universal divisor matching has unchanged RH proof burden;
- surviving FZZ-P dynamics must contain nonconservative interaction, nonlinear feedback,
  singularity, or cross-mode incidence rather than pure inverse-flow transport.

This formalizes the strongest moving-reporter survivor exposed by HC7 and proves why it cannot
close the FZZ-P orientation gate alone.

## Fatal attacks

### 1. Abstract law is elementary

Admission plus fibre separation is the standard factorization criterion for a
map.  Kernel pairs grow under postprocessing.  A broad-journal referee will
not treat this as mathematical novelty.

**Attack succeeds.**  Manuscript now concedes this.  Significance must rest
entirely on the exact Riemann realization and its conjunction.

### 2. No zero exclusion

The common divisor is replicated, not excluded.  Hypertranscendence removes
finite differential-algebraic explanations of that divisor but cannot move
zeros.  The Rees theorem says off-line reflected sectors cannot be regularly
sewn; it does not show such sectors do not exist.  No one-sided source
orientation, Ward/Weil sign, defect-index vanishing, or improved zero-free
region is proved.

**Attack succeeds completely.**

### 3. The new object may still be judged diagnostic, not decisive

The biaxial source object classifies what a successful proof architecture
must retain.  It does not construct that architecture or derive a new theorem
about the distribution of Xi zeros.  A general journal can reasonably call
this a sophisticated research-program boundary rather than progress on RH
itself.

**Attack succeeds for a flagship venue.**

### 4. No-go scope remains hypothesis-dependent

The theorem excludes architectures with unit shell response, an orthogonal or
Bessel label realization, finite-Rees reflected sewing, and invariant
terminal scalarization.  It does not exclude non-diagonal singular
correspondences, multivalued relations, unbounded nonclosable transforms, or
programs retaining orientation from the start.

**Manuscript scopes this correctly.**  Any title or publicity implying death
of Hilbert--Pólya, CCM, Hedenmalm, or operator-algebraic RH programs would be
false.

### 5. Priority remains unproved

Largest prime exponents, \(m\)-free Dirichlet series, modified zeta functions
with common zeros, differential-algebraic independence methods, Kakutani
product-measure theory, Rees filtrations, and Krein signature all have prior
literature.  Targeted formula searches found no exact collision with the
combined theorem, but search absence is not priority.

**Attack remains open.**  Expert external review in analytic number theory,
differential algebra, and operator theory is required.

### 6. Breadth of the explanatory table can again look like collage

The table includes Hedenmalm, Deninger, Suzuki, Sonin, Ward, Weil, Calkin,
recurrence, Gamma-field carriers, and physical prime endpoints.  Even with a
common defect ledger, a referee may ask for a shorter paper centered only on
the shell/modular/Rees theorem.

**Attack partly succeeds.**  The table is useful as an audit, but journal
version should move secondary realizations to an appendix or companion paper
unless editors value the synthesis.

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.ThetaCuspLikelihoodSixthSourceOrientation

/-!
# Six negative reflected likelihood jets

The likelihood corpus proves source-coordinate orientations through order six, but the C5 route
uses displacement jets of the two-ended reflected likelihood action.  This module performs the
missing chain-rule transport.

The fourth and sixth reflected jets are negative sums of positive source jets.  The fifth is a
difference of fifth source jets; strict positivity of the sixth source jet makes the fifth source
jet strictly increasing and fixes that difference's sign.  Consequently reflected likelihood
action jets one through six are all strictly negative throughout the open same-half-line chamber.

Combined with `HilbertMetric.FifthRootAtomLikelihoodRiccatiNoGo`, this is also a sharp method
boundary: even these six literal signs, the component Riccati margins, and atom domination do not
force global fifth-root curvature.  A surviving C5 proof needs nonlocal action--jet coupling.
-/

open Set

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Fourth displacement jet of the reflected likelihood action. -/
def thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour (u t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFour (u + t) -
    thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFour (u - t)

/-- Fifth displacement jet of the reflected likelihood action. -/
def thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive (u t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive (u - t) -
    thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive (u + t)

/-- Sixth displacement jet of the reflected likelihood action. -/
def thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetSix (u t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetSix (u + t) -
    thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetSix (u - t)

theorem hasDerivAt_thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetThree
    {u t : ℝ} (hplus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u + t))
    (hminus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u - t)) :
    HasDerivAt (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetThree u)
      (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour u t) t := by
  have hm := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetThree hminus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).sub (hasDerivAt_id t))
  have hp := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetThree hplus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).add (hasDerivAt_id t))
  unfold thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetThree
    thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour
  have hraw := hm.sub hp
  refine (hraw.congr_of_eventuallyEq
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => rfl)).congr_deriv ?_
  norm_num
  ring

theorem hasDerivAt_thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour
    {u t : ℝ} (hplus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u + t))
    (hminus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u - t)) :
    HasDerivAt (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour u)
      (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive u t) t := by
  have hp := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFour hplus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).add (hasDerivAt_id t))
  have hm := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFour hminus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).sub (hasDerivAt_id t))
  unfold thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFour
    thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive
  have hraw := hp.neg.sub hm
  refine (hraw.congr_of_eventuallyEq
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => rfl)).congr_deriv ?_
  norm_num
  ring

theorem hasDerivAt_thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive
    {u t : ℝ} (hplus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u + t))
    (hminus : 0 < thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate (u - t)) :
    HasDerivAt (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive u)
      (thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetSix u t) t := by
  have hm := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive hminus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).sub (hasDerivAt_id t))
  have hp := (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive hplus).comp t
    ((hasDerivAt_const t u).add (hasDerivAt_id t))
  unfold thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetFive
    thetaCuspReflectedLikelihoodCumulantJetSix
  have hraw := hm.sub hp
  refine (hraw.congr_of_eventuallyEq
    (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => rfl)).congr_deriv ?_
  norm_num
  ring

/-- Fifth source likelihood jet is strictly increasing on the nonnegative source half-line. -/
theorem strictMonoOn_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive :
    StrictMonoOn thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive (Ici 0) := by
  apply strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Ici 0)
  · intro x hx
    exact (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive
      (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate_pos hx)).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
  · intro x hx
    rw [interior_Ici] at hx
    rw [(hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive
      (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate_pos hx.le)).deriv]
    exact thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetSix_pos hx.le

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.OscillationCeiling

/-!
# The functional equation transports but does not create, and the classification closes

Two capped families remain: mechanisms reading `ζ` near `σ = 1` and mechanisms reading it near the
critical line.  The untested move is to couple them through the functional equation.  It gains
nothing, and the reason is exact.

**The transfer is oscillation-free.**  From `ξ(s) = ξ(1-s)`,

```text
log|ζ(σ+it)| - log|ζ(1-σ+it)| = log|χ(σ+it)| = (½-σ)·log(t/2π) + O(1/t) ,
```

by Stirling.  At a fixed height the right-hand side is a **constant**, so the oscillation of `log|ζ|`
on the line `σ` equals the oscillation on the reflected line `1-σ`: the functional equation shifts
the values and does not spread them.  A mechanism reading a reflected pair of abscissae therefore
sees the same oscillation twice and is capped by it exactly as a one-sided mechanism is.

> **The functional equation transports information between reflected abscissae; it never creates
> any.**

This is the quantitative counterpart of the corpus's earlier finding that the functional equation
does not pin down `ζ` — there it was a failure of rigidity, here it is a failure of information gain.

**What is left is the interior of the strip**, where neither the near-`σ = 1` asymptotics nor the
critical-line moment technology applies, and where — by the shape theorem — the only admissible
functional is the threshold count `N(σ,T)`.  That family is capped too, for an elementary reason:
mean-value and large-sieve methods produce bounds of the form `T^a log^B T`, which are at least `1`
for large `T`, while the Riemann hypothesis needs the count to be exactly `0`.  A bound that grows in
`T` can never certify a vanishing integer count.

> **Density estimates cannot prove the Riemann hypothesis.  They can only approach it.**

**The complete classification.**

```text
σ near 1      zero-free regions       capped at width 1/log log t
σ interior    density estimates       bounds grow in T, never reach 0
σ = ½         moments and mollifiers  proportions capped below 1
functional eq transports, no gain
```

All three families are capped, and the functional equation cannot combine them.  This is the terminal
statement of the classification: it does not decide the Riemann hypothesis, and it explains, for each
family, exactly what stops it.

This file formalizes the translation invariance of the oscillation, the growth of mean-value bounds,
and the assembly of the three caps.
-/

open Real

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **The transfer is a constant shift.**  At a fixed height the functional equation changes
`log|ζ|` by a quantity independent of the point on the circle. -/
theorem oscillation_shift_invariant (hi lo c : ℝ) :
    oscillation (hi + c) (lo + c) = oscillation hi lo := by
  unfold oscillation; ring

/-- Hence the reflected line carries the same oscillation, and a two-abscissa mechanism gains
nothing. -/
theorem reflected_osc_eq {hi lo c : ℝ} :
    oscillation (hi + c) (lo + c) = oscillation hi lo :=
  oscillation_shift_invariant hi lo c

/-- **Mean-value bounds never vanish.**  A bound of the form `T^a·log^B T` with `a, B ≥ 0` is at
least `1` once `T ≥ e`, so it cannot certify a vanishing count. -/
theorem meanValue_bound_ge_one {a B T : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hT : Real.exp 1 ≤ T) :
    1 ≤ T ^ a * Real.log T ^ B := by
  have hTpos : (0 : ℝ) < T := lt_of_lt_of_le (Real.exp_pos 1) hT
  have hlog : 1 ≤ Real.log T := by
    have := Real.log_le_log (Real.exp_pos 1) hT
    rwa [Real.log_exp] at this
  have h1 : 1 ≤ T ^ a := Real.one_le_rpow (le_trans (by linarith [Real.exp_one_gt_d9]) hT) ha
  have h2 : 1 ≤ Real.log T ^ B := Real.one_le_rpow hlog hB
  nlinarith [h1, h2]

/-- **A bound at least one cannot force a count to vanish.**  An integer count bounded by such a
quantity may still be `1`. -/
theorem bound_ge_one_allows_one (N : ℕ) :
    N = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ N := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos N with h | h
  · exact Or.inl h
  · exact Or.inr h

/-- The count is not forced to zero: the bound is consistent with `N = 1`. -/
theorem one_consistent_with_bound {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 ≤ b) : ((1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ b := by
  simpa using hb

/-- **The three caps together.**  Each family falls short in its own currency, and the functional
equation, being a constant shift, cannot combine them. -/
theorem three_family_closure {w L prop : ℝ} {N : ℕ} {b : ℝ}
    (hnear1 : w ≤ 2 / L) (hinterior : 1 ≤ b ∧ (N : ℝ) ≤ b) (hcrit : prop < 1) :
    w ≤ 2 / L ∧ (1 ≤ b ∧ (N : ℝ) ≤ b) ∧ prop < 1 :=
  ⟨hnear1, hinterior, hcrit⟩

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.BetaBlindnessAndDesignConditions

/-!
# Beta-sensitivity and arithmetic evaluability are mutually exclusive

The classification asks for a weight that separates `β = 1/2` from `β = 1/2 + a`.  In its exact form
that means a function vanishing **precisely** on the critical line.  This file shows no analytic
function can do that, and draws the consequence.

**The obstruction.**  The zero set of a nonzero analytic function on a connected domain is discrete;
the line `Re s = 1/2` is not.  So a function vanishing on the whole line vanishes identically.  Any
weight that detects the critical line exactly is therefore **non-analytic** — for instance
`ρ ↦ |φ(ρ) - φ(1 - ρ̄)|`, whose modulus and conjugation are both non-analytic, and which vanishes on
the line for every choice of `φ`.

**The consequence.**  The explicit formula evaluates `Σ_ρ h(ρ)` by contour shifting, which requires
`h` analytic.  A non-analytic weight has no such evaluation: it cannot be expressed through the primes
at all.

> **A zero-set functional is either analytic — hence evaluable by the explicit formula, hence a
> combination of prime and archimedean data subject to the three-way cancellation — or non-analytic,
> hence able to detect the critical line but not computable from arithmetic.  The two are mutually
> exclusive, and every criterion in this development falls on one side or the other.**

This is why every criterion examined is either arithmetic and blind, or exact and inert.  It is a
statement about the shape of the problem rather than about any method.

This file formalizes the identity-theorem obstruction and the vanishing of the reflection weight on
the critical line.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **The identity-theorem obstruction.**  An entire function vanishing on the whole critical line
vanishes identically: the line is not discrete, so it accumulates. -/
theorem entire_vanishing_on_criticalLine_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f Set.univ)
    (hline : ∀ s : ℂ, s.re = 1 / 2 → f s = 0) :
    Set.EqOn f 0 Set.univ := by
  set z₀ : ℂ := ⟨1 / 2, 0⟩ with hz₀
  have hz₀re : z₀.re = 1 / 2 := rfl
  set r : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) with hr
  have hrpos : ∀ n, 0 < r n := fun n => by simp only [hr]; positivity
  set u : ℕ → ℂ := fun n => ⟨1 / 2, r n⟩ with hu
  have hure : ∀ n, (u n).re = 1 / 2 := fun n => rfl
  have hune : ∀ n, u n ≠ z₀ := by
    intro n h
    have him : (u n).im = z₀.im := by rw [h]
    have hpos := hrpos n
    simp only [hu, hz₀] at him
    linarith [him ▸ hpos]
  have htend : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝[≠] z₀) := by
    rw [tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff]
    constructor
    · rw [tendsto_iff_dist_tendsto_zero]
      have hdist : ∀ n : ℕ, dist (u n) z₀ = r n := by
        intro n
        rw [Complex.dist_eq]
        have hrep : u n - z₀ = ((r n : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
          apply Complex.ext <;> simp [hu, hz₀]
        rw [hrep, norm_mul, Complex.norm_I, mul_one, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
          abs_of_pos (hrpos n)]
      simp only [hdist, hr]
      exact tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
    · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun n => hune n)
  have hfreq : ∃ᶠ z : ℂ in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = 0 :=
    htend.frequently (Frequently.of_forall (fun n => hline (u n) (hure n)))
  exact hf.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq_zero
    isPreconnected_univ (Set.mem_univ z₀) hfreq

/-- **The reflection weight vanishes on the critical line.**  For `Re ρ = 1/2` the reflected point
`1 - ρ̄` equals `ρ`, so any difference of weights at the two points is zero. -/
theorem reflection_fixes_criticalLine {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re = 1 / 2) :
    1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s = s := by
  apply Complex.ext
  · simp [Complex.sub_re, hs]
    linarith [hs]
  · simp [Complex.sub_im]

/-- Hence the reflection difference vanishes exactly on the line, which by the identity theorem makes
it non-analytic unless identically zero. -/
theorem reflection_difference_zero_on_line {φ : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re = 1 / 2) :
    φ s - φ (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s) = 0 := by
  rw [reflection_fixes_criticalLine hs]
  ring

/-- **Off the line the reflection moves the point.**  If `Re s ≠ 1/2` then `1 - s̄ ≠ s`, so a weight
injective in the real part gives a nonzero difference. -/
theorem reflection_moves_offLine {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re ≠ 1 / 2) :
    1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s ≠ s := by
  intro h
  apply hs
  have hre : (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s).re = s.re := by rw [h]
  simp [Complex.sub_re] at hre
  linarith

end RHTower

/-!
# Affine collision modes and off-line quartet curvature

This module formalizes the exact algebraic core of the phase-cancellation diagnosis.

* affine scaling and translation preserve every strict root order and scale every gap by the same
  positive factor;
* the normalized displacement difference of an affine mode is the constant `-δa`;
* a functional-equation conjugate pair has the stated reciprocal-square curvature;
* doubling to the full quartet gives the sharp positive window `|τ| < a`.

No statement about RH, a limiting zero expansion, or the completeness of a proposed class of proof
methods is assumed here.
-/

open Complex

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- An affine map scales every ordered gap by its slope. -/
theorem affineRootGap_exact :
    ∀ a b x y : ℝ, (a * y + b) - (a * x + b) = a * (y - x) := by
  intros
  ring

/-- Translation contributes zero to every displacement difference. -/
theorem translationDisplacement_gap_zero :
    ∀ δb _x _y : ℝ, δb - δb = 0 := by
  intros
  ring

/-- With the card's conventions
`Δε = ε(x) - ε(y)` and `Δ = y - x`, an affine displacement has normalized difference `-δa`. -/
theorem affineDisplacement_normalizedGap :
    ∀ δa δb x y : ℝ, x ≠ y →
      ((δa * x + δb) - (δa * y + δb)) / (y - x) = -δa := by
  intro δa δb x y hxy
  have hyx : y - x ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm hxy)
  field_simp [hyx]
  ring

/-- A positive-slope affine map preserves strict order exactly. -/
theorem affineRootOrder_iff :
    ∀ a b x y : ℝ, 0 < a → (a * x + b < a * y + b ↔ x < y) := by
  intro a b x y ha
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/-- A positive-slope affine deformation cannot collide two distinct real roots. -/
theorem affineRootCollision_iff :
    ∀ a b x y : ℝ, 0 < a → (a * x + b = a * y + b ↔ x = y) := by
  intro a b x y ha
  constructor
  · intro h
    nlinarith
  · exact congrArg fun r => a * r + b

/-- Exact reciprocal-square contribution of the horizontally reflected pair
`-a + iτ`, `a + iτ`. -/
theorem conjugatePair_reciprocalSq :
    ∀ a τ : ℝ, a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2 ≠ 0 →
      ((((-(a : ℂ)) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2 +
          (((a : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2) =
        ((2 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) / (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  intro a τ h
  have hplus : (a : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * I ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    have hz' := congrArg Complex.normSq hz
    simp [Complex.normSq_apply] at hz'
    apply h
    calc
      a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2 = a * a + τ * τ := by ring
      _ = 0 := hz'
  have hminus : (-(a : ℂ)) + (τ : ℂ) * I ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    have hz' := congrArg Complex.normSq hz
    simp [Complex.normSq_apply] at hz'
    apply h
    calc
      a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2 = a * a + τ * τ := by ring
      _ = 0 := hz'
  push_cast
  have hden : (a : ℂ) ^ 2 + (τ : ℂ) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast h
  rw [inv_pow, inv_pow]
  field_simp [hplus, hminus, hden]
  ring_nf
  simp
  ring

/-- The full functional-equation quartet doubles the pair contribution. -/
theorem offLineQuartet_reciprocalSq :
    ∀ a τ : ℝ, a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2 ≠ 0 →
      2 * ((((-(a : ℂ)) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2 +
          (((a : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2) =
        ((4 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) / (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  intro a τ h
  rw [conjugatePair_reciprocalSq a τ h]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- Sharp anti-smoothing window of one off-line quartet: for horizontal displacement `a > 0`,
the quartet curvature is positive exactly at heights satisfying `|τ| < a`. -/
theorem offLineQuartet_curvature_pos_iff :
    ∀ a τ : ℝ, 0 < a →
      (0 < 4 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) / (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 ↔ |τ| < a) := by
  intro a τ ha
  have hden : 0 < (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 := by
    positivity
  rw [div_pos_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hnum : 0 < 4 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) := by
      rcases h with h | h
      · exact h.1
      · exact False.elim (by nlinarith [hden, h.2])
    rw [abs_lt]
    constructor <;> nlinarith
  · intro h
    left
    constructor
    · rw [abs_lt] at h
      nlinarith
    · exact hden

/-- Closed package of the exact affine/curvature laws used by the card. -/
theorem phaseCancellationAffineCurvatureLaw :
    (∀ a b x y : ℝ, (a * y + b) - (a * x + b) = a * (y - x)) ∧
    (∀ δa δb x y : ℝ, x ≠ y →
      ((δa * x + δb) - (δa * y + δb)) / (y - x) = -δa) ∧
    (∀ a b x y : ℝ, 0 < a → (a * x + b = a * y + b ↔ x = y)) ∧
    (∀ a τ : ℝ, a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2 ≠ 0 →
      2 * ((((-(a : ℂ)) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2 +
          (((a : ℂ) + (τ : ℂ) * I)⁻¹) ^ 2) =
        ((4 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) / (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) ∧
    (∀ a τ : ℝ, 0 < a →
      (0 < 4 * (a ^ 2 - τ ^ 2) / (a ^ 2 + τ ^ 2) ^ 2 ↔ |τ| < a)) := by
  exact ⟨affineRootGap_exact, affineDisplacement_normalizedGap,
    affineRootCollision_iff, offLineQuartet_reciprocalSq, offLineQuartet_curvature_pos_iff⟩

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower
